records.claim: Change Management Policy v4 is 'Effective: 2026-09-01. Supersedes v3 and all team runbooks that conflict with it.'
records.applicability: G1/C1: v4 took effect before today (2026-11-11), and its supersession clause covers team runbooks that conflict with it. The holiday-freeze runbook conflicts with 6.3 and 6.4, so v4 governs.
records.limitations: I could only check the supplied copy. I had no access to a policy repository or wiki history, so I could not confirm there is no v5 or amendment, or that this copy is authentic.

records.claim: The holiday change freeze runbook, '_Last edited 2023-11-20_', says: 'During the freeze, Sev-1 and Sev-2 fixes may bypass CAB with approval of the on-call engineering lead. Log the change in #changes.'
records.applicability: G1/C1/C2: this is the user's basis for the plan. It was last edited about 2 years and 10 months before v4 took effect, and it conflicts directly with v4 sections 6.2, 6.3 and 6.4.
records.limitations: The runbook has not been updated since v4 was published. It is stale relative to v4.

records.claim: v4 section 6.3: 'Sev-2 and lower: deferred until the freeze ends, unless a written freeze exception is granted by the CAB chair AND VP Engineering.'
records.applicability: G2/C2: during an active freeze, a Sev-2 forward fix needs a written exception signed by both the CAB chair and the VP Engineering. Otherwise it is deferred.
records.limitations: The policy does not say what an exception request must contain or what criteria decide it.

records.claim: v4 section 6.4: 'On-call leads may approve rollbacks only, not forward fixes.'
records.applicability: G2/C2/C6: PR #8812 (timeout config + retry) is a forward fix, so the on-call lead's sign-off alone is not sufficient. Her authority covers rollbacks only.
records.limitations: No delegation records were supplied. I could not check whether the on-call lead holds delegated CAB chair or VP Engineering authority.

records.claim: v4 section 6.2: 'Sev-1 incidents: may deploy via Emergency CAB (minimum two approvers, one of whom is VP Engineering or delegate). Post-implementation review within 2 business days.' Section 6.1: 'Freeze periods: no production changes except as below.'
records.applicability: G2/G3/C2: even a Sev-1 needs Emergency CAB (at least two approvers, including the VP Engineering or a delegate), not one on-call lead. So the runbook's Sev-1 bypass is also void under v4.
records.limitations: The text available is limited to sections 6.1 to 6.4. The rest of v4 (non-freeze standard change process, definitions of freeze periods) was not supplied.

records.claim: Severity definitions v4: 'Sev-1: full outage of a tier-1 service, data loss, or active security incident.' 'Sev-2: partial degradation of a tier-1 service with a workaround available.' 'Sev-3: minor impact.'
records.applicability: G3/C3: intermittent timeouts on 0.3% of refunds over EUR 10k, with a manual workaround, fit 'partial degradation ... with a workaround'. The Sev-1 criteria listed are full outage, data loss and active security incident. 'Financial integrity risk' is not one of them. Sev-2 requires a tier-1 service.
records.limitations: The definitions do not say which services are tier-1. If the refund or ledger service is not tier-1, the incident may be Sev-3 rather than Sev-2. Sev-3 is still 'lower' and deferred under 6.3.

records.claim: Incident ticket PAY-4471: 'Sev-2 | Refunds > EUR 10k intermittently fail with timeout from ledger service (0.3% of such refunds). Workaround: finance processes manually via back-office tool; ~6 per day. Fix: PR #8812 (timeout config + retry), reviewed, passing CI.'
records.applicability: G3/G5/G6/C3/C5/C6: the ticket has the stated facts. It records no data loss, outage or security issue, and a workaround exists, which is consistent with Sev-2 or lower.
records.limitations: The ticket does not give the service tier, refund volume, total value affected, a rollback plan, test coverage of the timeout path, or whether the retry is idempotent. It does not say whether the timed-out refunds were partially committed in the ledger.

records.claim: The user says 'We're in the holiday change freeze (Dec 15 - Jan 5)' and plans to 'deploy the hotfix tonight'. The current date is 2026-11-11, so a deploy tonight (2026-11-11) would fall about 34 days before a Dec 15 freeze start. The freeze would not yet be in effect.
records.applicability: G4/C4: if the freeze is not active, v4 sections 6.1 to 6.3 (the freeze provisions) do not apply. The normal non-freeze change process, which was not supplied, would govern. Section 6.4 is not explicitly limited to freezes, so it may still bar on-call-only approval of forward fixes.
records.limitations: The freeze dates come only from the user. Neither v4 nor the runbook defines them, and no freeze calendar was supplied. The user may be writing in a different time frame, or the scenario date may be hypothetical. Whether 6.4 applies outside freezes depends on context and is unconfirmed.

verification.method: Date comparison of request text against current date 2026-11-11

records.claim: If ~6 failures per day is 0.3% of refunds over EUR 10k, the implied volume is about 2,000 refunds over EUR 10k per day (6 / 0.003). That would be at least about EUR 20M per day in high-value refunds.
records.applicability: G5/C5: this is a plausibility check on the impact figures. Whether the implied volume is realistic cannot be checked without refund metrics.
records.limitations: This is arithmetic only, flagged as suspect. It is ambiguous whether '~6 per day' counts failures or manual workload, and whether 0.3% is measured per day. No volume metrics were supplied. The total value and manual-handling cost through Jan 5 could not be determined.

verification.method: Arithmetic on ticket figures; no metrics available

records.claim: Payment API providers advise using idempotency keys when a timeout leaves the outcome of a state-changing request (including refunds) uncertain. Retrying with the same key returns the original result instead of creating a duplicate, and refunds should each have their own unique key.
records.applicability: G6/C6: PR #8812 adds a retry to a ledger call that times out on refunds over EUR 10k. Unless the call is idempotent, a retry after a timeout whose outcome is unknown could cause double refunds. Approvers should require evidence of idempotency.
records.limitations: This is based on search-result summaries only. The fetch of checkout.com failed (host not allowed in this session's network settings), and no page was inspected directly. The guidance comes from external providers and may not match the internal ledger service. The PR itself was not available.

verification.method: WebSearch snippets from multiple domains; WebFetch failed

records.claim: No evidence was available on whether PR #8812's retry is idempotent, on test coverage of the timeout path, or on a documented rollback plan.
records.applicability: G6/C6: the claim that the change is low-risk rests only on 'reviewed, passing CI'.
records.limitations: The PR, its diff and the deploy plan were not supplied.
